clue.text: Swallowed fish outside, battered perhaps

indicators.note: one word sits outside, wrapped round the other word

parts.note: a cod is a common fish
past tense of eat

explanation.surface: A fish swallows something whole, then ends up battered in a chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallowed fish' reads like a fish being eaten; the past-tense verb is the inner piece and the fish goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been battered has a covering of batter, so it is an example of something given a coating.

clue.text: Outcry at intrigue after half the club has departed

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, the rest being dropped

parts.note: taken as written
an amour is a love affair, especially a secret one

explanation.surface: Members protest at scheming once half the club has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: An intrigue can mean a clandestine love affair, which is why it matches the French loan word.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud public protest or uproar, which is a synonym for an outcry.

clue.text: Shrewd one wants to get lovable

parts.note: one can be read as the article a
cute means charming or lovable

explanation.surface: A shrewd person aims to come across as endearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute mind is sharp and perceptive, so the adjective is a synonym of shrewd.

clue.text: Adorable when close round ear

indicators.note: a word placed round another wraps itself about it

parts.note: a close is a conclusion
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something looks sweet when held close to someone's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like the adjective meaning near, but it is the noun meaning a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endearing inspires affection, so it is close in sense to adorable.

clue.text: A child, one with the first girl to win

parts.note: taken as written
CH is a standard abbreviation for child
the Roman numeral for one
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A child and the first girl team up hoping to win something.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve a goal or victory is to gain it, so the verb is a synonym of win in that sense.

clue.text: Mean and undistinguished

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the arithmetic mean of a set of numbers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as stingy or nasty; here it is the statistical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the statistical midpoint of a set and also describes something ordinary and unremarkable.

clue.text: Dream up headgear to go on child

parts.note: a hat is worn on the head
CH is a standard abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: Someone invents a hat to sit on a child's head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece going on another sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hatch a plan is an idiom for devising or inventing it, the same as dreaming one up.

clue.text: Mysterious model came with gin and it

indicators.note: to model is to shape material into a new form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mysterious fashion model arrives carrying gin and Italian vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun for a person; it is a verb. Gin and it is a classic cocktail, 'it' being Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enigmatic is puzzling and hard to interpret, so it is a synonym of mysterious.

clue.text: Polishes me up on issues

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word me read upwards
ends are outcomes or results, things that issue

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up their own writing on certain topics.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it, which is polishing it in the editorial sense.

clue.text: Antelopes, half crazy, retreating but forgotten

indicators.note: something retreating goes back the way it came, so it reads in the opposite direction
only half of the word is kept and the remainder is dropped

parts.note: gnus are African antelopes, also called wildebeest
nuts means mad

explanation.surface: A herd of half-mad antelopes retreats and is soon forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the first half of the slang word for mad, add it after the antelopes, then read the whole string upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsung heroes are those whose deeds go uncelebrated, so the word means overlooked or forgotten.

clue.text: Wealth of one taking cake at the ball

parts.note: one can be read as the article a
a bun is a small cake
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A wealthy guest helps themselves to cake at a grand ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealth of something means a great quantity of it, which is what plenty or profusion means.

clue.text: Just a moment to get rice on time

indicators.note: placing one thing on another here means it follows it, so the grain word comes second

parts.note: T is the usual abbreviation for time
taken as written; that the letters also run across the end of 'get rice' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Cooking rice on a timer only takes a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here means the rice word is placed after the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In a trice is an idiom for in an instant, so the word names a very brief space of time.

clue.text: Entertainment: a short work, but taking time

parts.note: op. is the short form of opus, a musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A brief piece of entertainment that nonetheless drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that opera is famously long, though built from the short form of a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged musical drama is one kind of theatrical entertainment, so this is an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Honest girl meets fake journalist

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
a sham is a fake
ED, short for editor

explanation.surface: A truthful young woman encounters a phoney reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without shame is open and unembarrassed about what they do, close to being candid or frank.

clue.text: Car reversed by bigwig needs support

indicators.note: the word for the vehicle is to be read from its end back to its start

parts.note: the word car written backwards
a king is a very important person

explanation.surface: A VIP's car has been reversed and now needs propping up.
explanation.definitionFit: Racking is a framework of racks or shelving that holds things up, so it is a kind of support.

clue.text: Top account promises to be large

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
AC is the abbreviation for account
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A leading financial account pledges to grow large.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capacious has room for a lot, so it is roomy or large in capacity.

clue.text: Card game, one discovered in the ruins of Crete

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found sitting inside it
a ruined building has its parts scattered, so the letters of the island are broken up

parts.note: the Greek island, taken as written
one can be read as the article a

explanation.surface: An archaeologist unearths an ancient playing card among Cretan ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Écarté is a nineteenth-century card game for two players, an example of the general category.

clue.text: Anyone present could make this loser calm

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something else by rearranging them

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Anyone who shows up might soothe a sore loser.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition open to all comers welcomes anyone who turns up, so the phrase names everyone present.

clue.text: Drunkard, full of pork, needs a tap

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside itself

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker
pork is meat from a pig

explanation.surface: A drunk, stuffed with pork, wants a tap of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a small tap or peg controlling the flow from a cask, so it is a synonym for that valve.

clue.text: Dishonoured one in the can with Edward

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a tin is a can
one can be read as the article a
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A disgraced man is in prison alongside Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the can' is slang for in prison, which colours the surface; here the can is just a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A tainted reputation is stained or sullied, so tainted carries the sense of disgraced.

clue.text: Aquatic bird no longer in place

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large water bird with a throat pouch
second meaning: the British pedestrian crossing of this name, being phased out and replaced

explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with push-button lights; councils have been removing them in favour of newer puffin and toucan crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the literal sense; the second hint relies on the crossing type that is disappearing from British streets.

clue.text: Bear-like creatures turning over in sorry sleep

indicators.note: turning something over flips it so it reads the other way round

parts.note: sad means sorry or regretful
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Bears roll over fitfully in a sad, uneasy sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandas look like bears and are often called bears, so the phrase describes them.

clue.text: No partners want child that can't slide

parts.note: taken as written
North and South are partners in bridge
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: Couples without a child to look after, who cannot slip away.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the players sitting North and South form one partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-skid surface or tyre grips well and resists slipping, so it describes something that won't slide.

clue.text: Criticise a mother's hat

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
taken as written
Ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a mum's choice of hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight straw hat, so it is one example of the wider category.

clue.text: Coin cases mistakenly forming new item for a collection

indicators.note: something done mistakenly comes out wrong, so the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A numismatist mixes up their coin cases while adding a new piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Museums and libraries record each newly acquired object as an accession, the technical term for an addition.

clue.text: Complicated fears keep one more secure

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tangled anxieties make a person play it safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Safer is the comparative of safe, and safe means secure, so it equals more secure.

clue.text: This head could make one cry

definitions.text: This head could make one cry

parts.words: This head could make one cry
parts.note: surface reading: someone's head, perhaps a stern headteacher, reducing a person to tears; setter's reading: a bulb of a vegetable, which releases eye-stinging vapour when chopped

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a person's head or a school head; it is the round bulb of a kitchen vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting this bulb releases a sulphur compound that irritates the eyes and makes cooks weep.

clue.text: Angry buccaneer beheaded

indicators.note: removing the head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a buccaneer is a pirate

explanation.surface: A furious pirate has been executed by beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very annoyed or furious, a straightforward synonym of angry.

clue.text: A fool turning backwards is stand-offish

indicators.note: turning to face backwards means the word is read from end to start

parts.note: taken as written
the word fool written backwards

explanation.surface: A silly person turns their back on people, looking haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: An aloof person keeps their distance and is cool and reserved, which is what being stand-offish means.

clue.text: Logo suggests job with quality

parts.note: a trade is an occupation
a mark is a distinguishing quality or characteristic

explanation.surface: A company logo is meant to convey skilled work of high quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A registered symbol identifying a company's goods is a trademark, and a logo is a common form of one.

clue.text: Confident nitwit angry about upper class

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
U is the old label for upper-class usage
seeing red means being angry

explanation.surface: A self-assured fool gets cross about posh people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal, but the upper-class letter simply comes before the colour; read it loosely as 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: An assured manner is self-confident and certain, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: There's just nothing at the street edge here in Belgium

parts.note: the figure zero, nothing
ST is the abbreviation for street
an end is an edge or extremity

explanation.surface: Someone notes there is nothing at the edge of a street in a Belgian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a port town on the Belgian coast, so it is a place found in that country.
